question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true about the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}\,{e}^{x/y}?$

I. Both partial derivatives exist at the point $(1,1)$

II. ${f}_{x}(0,1)$ is defined

III. ${f}_{y}(0,1)$ is defined
question.worked_solution:
First, we compute the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}\sqrt{x}\,{e}^{x/y} \\  & ={e}^{x/y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x})+\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x/y}) \\  & ={e}^{x/y}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}+\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{{e}^{x/y}}{y} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x/y}(2x+y)}{2y\sqrt{x}} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}\sqrt{x}\,{e}^{x/y} \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x/y}) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot {e}^{x/y}\cdot (-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}\,{e}^{x/y}}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's examine the statements one-by-one.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the function $f$ is defined at $(1,1)$, where we have 

$$
f(1,1)=\sqrt{1}\,{e}^{1/1}=e,
$$

and both partial derivatives are also defined at $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,1) & =\frac{{e}^{1/1}(2(1)+1)}{2(1)\sqrt{1}}=\frac{3e}{2} \\ {f}_{y}(1,1) & =-\frac{\sqrt{{1}^{3}}\,{e}^{1/1}}{{1}^{2}}=-e\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. If we substitute $(0,1)$ into ${f}_{x}$, we get

$$
{f}_{x}(0,1)=\frac{{e}^{0/1}(2(0)+1)}{2(1)\sqrt{0}}=\frac{1}{0},
$$

which is undefined since we have division by zero.

- Statement III is true. Indeed, the function $f$ itself is defined at $(0,1)$, where we have 

$$
f(0,1)=\sqrt{0}\,{e}^{0/1}=0,
$$

and ${f}_{y}$ is also defined at $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(0,1)=-\frac{\sqrt{{0}^{3}}\,{e}^{0/1}}{{1}^{2}}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
